To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the theory of supervisory controllability of real-time systems has been extended to a general model of real time where time is continuous and the event occurrence time sets can be arbitrary sets, (2) the real-time controllable and real-time controllably implementable sets are characterized in terms of the real-time contollability condition, (3) the real-time language of a real-time controllable real-time implementable system is characterized by a real-time implementation of the system,
the theory of supervisory discrete event systems is applicable to the real-time systems and the controllability of a discrete event system can be extended to the real time setting.
(1) The real-time controllabiltiy condition is a sufficient condition for the existence and uniqueness of a real-time supervisor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a supervisory framework for the real-time setting and the development of the theory for this setting.
the synthesis of real-time supervisors that can be implemented on real-time systems.
the development of supervisory control theory for real-time discrete event systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a supervisor achieving the desired behavior exists if and only if the real-time controllable and real-time observable languages are equal.
the real-time controllable language is a subset of the controllable language and the real-time controller language is a subset (not necessarily proper) of the controllable real-time language.
a supervisor achieving a given real-time behavior exists if and only if the real-time behavior can be obtained by a prioritized synchronous composition of the plant with some other timed automaton.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we provide a framework to control a real-time system by a supervisor which is a real-time timed automaton and we also provide a sufficient controllability condition for the existence for the real-time supervisor.
we have developed a theory for supervisory control of timed systems.
the theory of supervisory real-time discrete event systems is developed and a method for the synthesis of a supervisor is provided for achieving a desired timed specification.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the theory of supervisory contol can be extended to the real time setting.
the theory of supervisory controllers can be extended to the real- time setting and the real-time control problem is solvable in a similar manner to the untimed control problem.
real-time supervisory control is feasible and can be used to control the real-time behavior of systems.
